name: Fanatics
summary: Fanatics is a global sports platform spanning licensed merchandise, collectibles, betting and events. Its latest disclosed equity round raised about $700 million at a $31 billion valuation in December 2022.
overview: Fanatics has expanded from licensed sports merchandise into trading cards and collectibles, betting and gaming, events, and a wider sports-commerce ecosystem.

facts.label: Latest disclosed equity financing
facts.note: Fanatics published the Wall Street Journal report on the funding; no later priced equity round was located.

bull_case: Exclusive sports rights, owned collectibles and an expanding digital ecosystem can give Fanatics a rare, multi-category relationship with fans and leagues.
bear_case: The platform combines businesses with different economics, while collectibles, betting and sports retail face cyclical demand, regulatory and execution risk.
directory_notes: Licensed merchandise, collectibles, betting and events
Watch rights renewal, collectibles economics and regulated-market expansion.

intelligence.description: Sports-commerce platform spanning licensed merchandise, trading cards and collectibles, betting, gaming and live events.

metrics.label: Founded
metrics.note: Michael Rubin acquired the business in 2011

company: Fanatics operates licensed sports merchandise, trading cards and collectibles through Topps, betting and gaming products, and fan events. Its strategy is to connect league and athlete rights with direct fan distribution across several categories.

In December 2022, Fanatics raised about $700 million at a $31 billion valuation, according to a Wall Street Journal report published by the company. Its subsequent expansion has included new collectibles partnerships and a 2026 agreement to acquire BGC assets for a prediction-market exchange.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Fanatics is an unusual private-company case: a consumer platform built around scarce sports rights rather than a single product category. The key question is whether the shared customer, data and licensing infrastructure produces durable cross-sell economics across commerce, collectibles and regulated gaming.

changed.text: Raised about $700M at a $31B valuation, according to the Wall Street Journal.
Announced an agreement to acquire a contract market and clearinghouse from BGC for a prediction-market exchange.

takeaways: The latest disclosed $31B valuation dates to 2022, not a current market mark.
Long-term sports rights and direct-to-fan distribution are the core strategic assets.
Collectibles and betting can expand the platform, but add cyclicality and regulation.
